**Full Professor of Statistics and Operations Research**

<p class="lead">Artificial Intelligence · Bayesian and spatio-temporal statistics · Efficiency and productivity</p>

<p class="affiliation"><strong>i-MInD</strong> — <span lang="es">Instituto en Matemáticas, Inteligencia Artificial y Ciencia de Datos</span><br>Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche, Spain</p>

I research statistical and Artificial Intelligence methods and transfer them into practical applications. My work combines Bayesian modelling, spatial and spatio-temporal statistics, and machine learning to quantify uncertainty and support decision making.

I collaborate with researchers, companies and public institutions in health, ecology, environmental science and economics. With Juan Aparicio and colleagues, I develop methods and software for efficiency and productivity analysis.

<div class="topics"><a href="cva.html#artificial-intelligence">Artificial Intelligence papers</a><a href="cva.html#spatial-statistics">Spatial statistics</a><a href="cva.html#efficiency-productivity">Efficiency &amp; productivity</a></div>

## Artificial Intelligence in research and knowledge transfer

My research includes machine learning for species distribution and clinical prediction, Bayesian networks, and learning methods for production frontiers. My knowledge-transfer activity includes applied statistical and AI consulting, open-source software, and training in generative AI for public administrations.

[Explore research and knowledge transfer](xbarber.html) · [Read my CV and selected publications](cva.html)

## Selected research highlights

- **Spatial modelling:** [disease modelling under spatial misalignment](https://doi.org/10.4081/gh.2016.415) and [multivariate bioclimatic models](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13253-018-00345-z).
- **Efficiency and productivity:** [production functions based on regression splines](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2023.06.035) and the [`eat` R package](https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2022-054), with Juan Aparicio and colleagues.
- **Interdisciplinary impact:** [BIMCV COVID-19+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01174), a preprint describing an imaging dataset, and the [large-scale population survey of the COVID-19 pandemic in Spain](https://doi.org/10.2196/21319).

## Beyond research

I am from Dénia, Spain. I graduated in Statistics in 2000 and completed my PhD in 2009, supervised by Javier Morales and Antonio López-Quílez. Outside work, I enjoy rowing, cycling with my grupetta, and the music of Motörhead.
